text:
natalie: Heads-up: last night deploybot pushed runtime-2.16.0 to canary (asia-south) and auto-applied a hard-pin for model 'embedder-lite' due to kernel mismatch. We're seeing embedding cosine drift vs baseline and a few downstream ranking flaps.

deploybot: Deploy event: runtime-2.16.0 -> canary started 2026-03-23T02:10Z. Pin: hard, scope=cohort=canary, model=embedder-lite. Observability tags: embeddings, tokenization. https://deploy.redwood/6161623456 :robot_face:

ryan: Noted. Can you share the drift numbers? how big is the cosine change?

natalie: Quick metric snapshot: cosine mean delta ~ -0.018, 99th percentile delta -0.045 on our eval set (20k queries). Ranking recall@10 dropped ~1.5% for a small test customer.

jia: SDK note: sdk-py 0.22.0 includes a tokenization normalization change that pairs with runtime-2.16). If customers use older SDKs they may see mismatch. We should add compat guidance.

ops-sre: Given ranking impact, recommend converting hard-pin -> soft-pin and enable gradual fallback to runtime-2.15 for embedding routes while we triage. Propose routing patch: ```json
{"routes": [{"if": "model=='embedder-lite' && region=='asia-south'","to": "runtime-2.15","weight": 0.2},{"else":"runtime-2.16"}]}
```
I can stage this to canary in 5m.

ryan: +1 flip to soft-pin. Also run an eval with tokenization normalization disabled to see if SDK change explains drift.

sam: I'll draft a short note in release-notes/2.16.0: "Embedding parity: runtime-2.16 changes token normalization for embedder-lite; customers using custom tokenizers or sdk-py<0.22.0 might observe small embedding deltas. Recommended mitigation: upgrade SDK or set fallback routing." Also ping targeted Dedicated customers.

natalie: Good. Any risk of rollback? If we go soft-pin and fallback weight 0.2 for runtime-2.15, we should monitor recall@10 and embed delta. If delta persists >0.02 at 30m, auto-rollback to 2.15 (deploybot hook).

deploybot: Scheduled action: convert hard-pin -> soft-pin for cohort=canary at 02:40Z. Will apply fallback weight 0.2 to runtime-2.15. Auto-rollback trigger: recall@10 drop >1% sustained 10m OR embedding-delta mean <-0.02 over 5m.

ops-sre: Alerting rule set. I'll add a temporary eval job that computes recall@10 every 2m and a canary health dashboard. If triggers, deploybot will run rollback job: `deploybot rollback --target runtime-2.15 --scope cohort=canary`.

ryan: I kicked off the tokenization-disabled eval against a canary pod. Results: when we disable new normalization, mean embedding delta ~ -0.002 (within noise). That suggests SDK/normalization interplay.

jia: Ok - that points to client-side upgrade being required. Can we push a console banner and a short migration snippet for sdk-py? Something like: "If you use embedder-lite on runtime-2.16, upgrade sdk-py to 0.22.0 or set header X-RW-KV-NORM=legacy for parity."

sam: Will add banner + migration snippet and create a docs PR. Also adding an entry to support playbook for Dedicated customers: steps to enable fallback routing or pin back to 2.15.

natalie: Summary plan: 1) change hard-pin -> soft-pin immediately (deploybot action) 2) add fallback routing weight 0.2 to runtime-2.15 for embedder-lite in asia-south 3) push console banner + release note edit calling out sdk-py 0.22.0 4) monitor recall/embed delta and auto-rollback threshold 5) targeted customer comms if any Dedicated customers in region see regression.

ops-sre: Done: pin converted to soft at 02:41Z, fallback route applied. Watchlist and alerting active.

ryan: Monitoring: after fallback applied, recall@10 drop reduced to 0.4% and embedding mean delta -0.006. Looks acceptable.

jia: I'll coordinate a small migration test with the SDK team to publish a compatibility note and a quick fix snippet for self-hosted tokenizers.

sam: Release notes updated and PR filed: https://docs.redwood/changes/2.16.0. I'm sending a quick note to accounts with Dedicated in asia-south.

natalie: Thanks everyone. We'll keep this on watch for 2 hours then remove the soft-pin if stable. Will post final status in eng-releases. :white_check_mark:
